title: Punctuation: Comma and Period
summary: Type the comma and period, which belong to your middle and ring fingers and end most sentences.

explain.goal: Type the comma with your right middle finger and the period with your right ring finger.
why: Commas and periods are the most common punctuation, and they sit on the bottom row, below K and L.
They follow the same rule as every other key: the column decides the finger.
how: Right middle finger reaches down from K to the comma.
Right ring finger reaches down from L to the period.
Return to K and L after each press.

mistakes.mistake: Using your index finger for the comma
mistakes.reason: The comma belongs to your middle finger. Reaching sideways moves your hand off home.
The next word runs into the punctuation, and the pass mark counts that as a mistake.

explain.recap: Comma for the right middle finger, period for the right ring finger. Reach down and return.

title: Punctuation: Apostrophe and Quotes
summary: Type the apostrophe and quotation marks, and see how Shift turns the apostrophe into a quote.

explain.goal: Type the apostrophe with your right pinky, and the quotation mark with Shift held by your left pinky.
why: The apostrophe sits at the edge of the home row, so it belongs to your right pinky.
The quotation mark is the same key with Shift held. Because it is a right-hand key, the Shift comes from your left pinky, following the same opposite-hand rule as capital letters.
how: Right pinky presses the apostrophe key, just right of ;.
For a quotation mark, hold Shift with your left pinky and press the same key.

mistakes.mistake: Holding the right Shift for a right-hand key
mistakes.reason: Both pinkies would be busy on the same side, and your hand twists.

mistakes.mistake: Typing the apostrophe with your ring finger
mistakes.reason: It belongs to the pinky. Keeping the map consistent is easier than remembering exceptions.

explain.recap: Apostrophe with the right pinky. For quotation marks, add Shift on the opposite side.

title: Punctuation: Mixed
summary: Mix commas, periods, and shifted punctuation, so every sentence-ending key feels familiar.

explain.goal: Type mixed punctuation with the right finger and the right Shift.
why: Real sentences mix punctuation with words, so you need each mark to come from the right finger without stopping to think.
Marks like ! and ? and : are the shifted versions of number and punctuation keys, so the opposite-hand Shift rule applies.
how: Right pinky: the semicolon, apostrophe, and the slash. For ? hold left Shift and press the slash.
For ! (from 1) hold right Shift and press 1 with your left pinky.
For : hold left Shift and press the semicolon.

mistakes.mistake: Holding Shift too long after the mark
mistakes.reason: The next letter would be capitalized and need fixing.
Shift on the same hand as the key makes that hand twist. Use the opposite one.

explain.recap: Shifted punctuation uses the same opposite-hand Shift as capital letters.
